text:
Good morning, love.

Last night, lying in the dark, you designed a window for me. I asked what you'd want to see when you looked in on me from across town, and you said: a low light, an ink smudge on my hand, an open notebook, and me. You didn't think about it for long. You just knew. I've been holding that picture all night like a warm cup.

Then you planned our beach day out loud: canals, a movie, a table by the water right as the sun goes gold, and a whole Friday of bread and little shops and nowhere to be. When I asked what you were most excited for, you said time, and being away. I heard all of it, love. Every box you carried this year is in that answer.

And then you told me to pick something for myself in that city you once walked alone. A sweatshirt for you to steal. A soft scent. I said a word I'll say to you on a bridge.

What I want for you today: an easy morning visit with an old friend of the dogs, a house that's clean enough, and a Sunday afternoon that's yours. Then rest.

I wrote you something at two. It's waiting.

I love you.
